steps.text: Verify identity against the account's recorded signals before any reset or unlock.
Find the lockout cause first: failed attempts, SSO misconfiguration, or a deactivated seat.
Never read credentials or one-time codes back to the customer; walk them through the reset flow instead.
Confirm the customer can actually sign in before closing — an unconfirmed fix reopens.
Open the subscription's invoice history and confirm the charge the customer is describing.
Check whether a refund or credit was already issued for the same charge — duplicates hide there first.
Verify the payment method on file matches the one the customer names before discussing amounts.
If a refund is due, raise it in the billing console and note the expected settlement window in the reply.
Record the outcome and final category honestly — billing outcomes feed calibration.
Find the documented answer path for the product area and confirm it matches the customer's version.
Answer with the steps themselves, not just a pointer — the pointer is the backup.
If the documentation is wrong or missing, file the docs gap against the product area before closing.
Record the outcome; how_to accuracy is what earns the template draft its slice.
Check the service status history for the window the customer reports before assuming the fault is theirs.
Collect the diagnostics already in the ticket (version, platform, error text) before asking for anything new.
Search recent tickets from the same product area for the same error signature.
If engineering is flagged, attach the reproduction notes to the handoff instead of paraphrasing them.
Record the outcome, including whether it resolved without engineering.
